_doc: Every table an applied migration inserts into at migration time, classified.
ops/snapshot_seed_coverage.py refuses to let bin/schema-snapshot.sh write a file
while any such table is missing from both lists, because that is the shape of the
five traps already patched by hand: the ledger says the migration ran, so its seed
never replays, and a rebuilt database has the table and none of its rows.
CARRIED means the snapshot must contain its rows and the check asserts they are there.
Adding to this list is NOT this file's decision to make on its own: the rule in
bin/schema-snapshot.sh still governs it — a table qualifies because someone read its
rows and can say what is in them, never because a migration seeded it. Adding a table
here without also adding the block that emits it makes the snapshot refuse, which is
the intended order: decide, then carry.
EXCLUDED means a rebuild is correct without those rows. Excluding is the safe
direction - the cost of a wrong exclusion is the status quo, while the cost of a wrong
carry is client or runtime data in a tracked file. Each entry says why.
CARRIED_SUBSET means the table is carried in part by a scoped render because it holds
two kinds of row. It must be present, and the reason states the scope.
CARRIED_AFTER_APPLY is for a reviewed bounded seed whose source migration is
not yet in the snapshot ledger. It must be absent while pending and becomes
row-required automatically when the migration enters the ledger.

carried_after_apply.ops.canonical_ownership_issuer_generatio: 0532a's exact two-principal issuer selector: repository-owned g1 is active and g2 is draining. These are bounded control configuration and the foreign-key target for canonical ownership runtime sessions, not session records or credentials. Once the migration enters the snapshot ledger, bin/schema-snapshot.sh verifies and carries only these two rows.
carried_after_apply.ops.completion_policy: the single versioned completion-default policy seeded by migration 0431; it contains only tenant metadata, the closed required-dimension list, freshness, precedence, effective time, and its digest. Without it the completion projection has no policy and emits no subjects. Carried by an exact source-verified block in bin/schema-snapshot.sh; no subjects, observations, relations, dispositions, or receipts are carried
carried_after_apply.ops.engineering_stale_contract_fence: 0532a's exact two-row, append-only stale-contract deny-list. It contains only burned work-request/plan identifiers, hashes, migration filenames, successor flags and reasons; no client, runtime session, credential, or execution record. Once its migration enters the snapshot ledger, bin/schema-snapshot.sh verifies and carries the two reviewed fence rows so old contracts stay refused after rebuild.
carried_after_apply.ops.scac_mutation_registry_entry: the immutable v1-v9 SCAC mutation inventory entries seeded by migrations 0454 through 0468. They are bounded internal security configuration, contain source contracts and catalog ACL projections rather than business or runtime data, and are required for every exact registry lookup. Carried with their sealed version headers by a source-verified block in bin/schema-snapshot.sh once 0468 enters the snapshot ledger
carried_after_apply.ops.scac_mutation_registry_version: the nine immutable v1-v9 SCAC registry seal headers seeded by migrations 0454 through 0468. They are bounded internal security configuration and the foreign-key parents and cryptographic seals for ops.scac_mutation_registry_entry. Carried with the exact entry rows by a source-verified block in bin/schema-snapshot.sh once 0468 enters the snapshot ledger
carried_after_apply.ops.slice_marker_seat: 0626's two automated slice-marker seat rows (joe-local, dell-local): internal machine-actor slugs and a one-line note each; no client, party, deal, event or credential. The seat doors refuse every actor not in it, so a rebuild without these rows would silently stop the slice done-record from ever firing. Pending until 0626 enters the snapshot ledger; bin/schema-snapshot.sh carries it with the reference vocabulary dump

carried.activity_kind: closed vocabulary, foreign-key target; bounded vocabulary pg_dump
carried.actor: internal actor identities (joe, dell, system, automation) that events point at
carried.agent_profile: A MIGRATION-SEEDED REGISTRY WITH NO RUNTIME WRITER, and the earlier reason here was wrong on the facts. 0284 seeds the named profiles; nothing inserts the table at runtime — mcp-server/src/agent-profiles.js only UPDATEs, and mcp-server/src/bot-brief.js THROWS profile_not_found when a profile is missing, its own hint saying 'new profiles are a migration'. The previous entry claimed that file tolerates an empty set, which it does not. A rebuild without these rows makes the bot brief fail for every named profile. Read before carrying: profile_key, display_name, a charter of role sentences, status — no client, party, deal or event content. Loud rather than silent, unlike the doctrine registry, but the same wrong-premise shape
carried.client_status: closed vocabulary; client.status is a foreign key to it
carried.deal_phase: the eight closed deal phases; foreign-key target
carried.doctrine_edge_type: closed vocabulary of doctrine graph edges
carried.doctrine_gate_check: THE DOCTRINE VALIDATION REGISTRY, not gate results — those are doctrine_gate_finding and doctrine_gate_run. Its own comment in 0075 states the contract: 'A NEW GATE IS A FUNCTION AND A ROW.' 0075 seeds 11 rows, all severity=block and enabled, and nothing writes the table at runtime. Its only consumer is runGates() in mcp-server/src/doctrine.js, which selects the enabled checks — so a database rebuilt without them loads an empty registry, produces no findings, and lets EVERY doctrine write pass with no gate run at all. Read before carrying: check_key, severity, impl_key and a one-line description, no client, party, deal or event content. An earlier revision of this file excluded it as 'runtime evidence', which was simply wrong, and that wrong exclusion was the seventh instance of the trap this check exists to catch
carried.doctrine_meta: singleton bootstrap row appended as deterministic SQL, not vocabulary
carried.ops.enforcement_control_catalog: reviewed controls rendered from the repository's own declarations; without them 0228 cannot validate pinned rules
carried.ops.execution_environment_conformance: governed execution seeds appended as deterministic SQL (0309)
carried.ops.execution_environment_provider: governed execution seeds appended as deterministic SQL (0309)
carried.ops.execution_environment_provider_event: governed execution seeds appended as deterministic SQL (0309)
carried.ops.guidance_registry: the registry's own singleton header row; guidance-registry-db-gate fails without it
carried.ops.job_definition: the two fixed internal job contracts (renewal-radar-source-daily, governed execution); never widened to arbitrary job rows
carried.ops.rule_delivery_activation_target: the exact ledger-appropriate reviewed cutover targets; without them a rebuild has no cutover target set
carried.ops.rule_delivery_policy: bounded singleton delivery policy; without it a rebuild comes up mode:null
carried.ops.siep_component_alias: the 25 SCAC/MPE component aliases. The same db-gate asserts the exact alias mapping against its reviewed manifest; carried by the sealed-restore block, digest-verified at load
carried.ops.siep_package_contract: the 40 reviewed SIEP package contracts. ops/siep-program-local-pg-gate.py asserts the exact package set, so a rebuild without them fails that db-gate; carried by the sealed-restore block, digest-verified at load
carried.ops.siep_program_dependency: the 88-edge SIEP dependency DAG. The same db-gate asserts all 88 edges exactly and fails on any drift; carried by the sealed-restore block, digest-verified at load
carried.retrieval_proposal: 0135's ten pending seed proposals; situation-retrieval-db-gate expects exactly ten
carried.retrieval_ranking_policy: the two versioned ranking policies; the active row carries the golden_suite_digest the assertion looks up

carried_subset.ops.work_request: CARRIED IN PART, SIEP program rows only: the ops.work_request rows that ops.siep_package_contract.work_request_id points at, restored by the SIEP manifest block in bin/schema-snapshot.sh with the insert guards and seals disabled for the restore and the manifest digest asserted afterwards. Those rows are internal program configuration created by 0324's own literal package list: requester and owner 'joe', no client, party, deal, event, doctrine or credential reference, and their only outbound foreign key is public.actor, which this snapshot already carries. NEVER the sourced captures (WR-000001 onward) - those are operational history.

excluded.ops.rule_insert_provenance: rule INSERT transaction identities — runtime provenance local to one live database; xid8 values must never be restored into a new database
excluded.agent_profile_assignment: A RULING LEDGER, append-only, and the earlier reason here was wrong on the facts. It said 0284's immutability probe was the only migration-time insert; 0300 also seeds EIGHT permanent rows - the Hermes operational roster, with fixed idempotency keys, ruling_basis 'human', and its own assertion that all eight exist. So this table IS seeded, and the exclusion has to stand on what the rows are FOR rather than on a claim that they do not exist. Nothing selects it: mcp-server/src/agent-profiles.js only INSERTs (the assign-profile verb), and no gate, verb or view reads it back. A rebuild without these rows therefore loses the recorded history of who assigned which model to which desk, and breaks nothing at runtime - unlike agent_profile, which is carried because bot-brief THROWS profile_not_found without it. Read before excluding: profile_id, model, desk, status, who ruled and on what basis. Excluded as history, not as absence.
excluded.client: client records — the business data this snapshot exists to keep out of git
excluded.deal_reattach_log: a record of deal reattachments performed on production — business history
excluded.marketing_subject: marketing subjects pointing at clients and deals — business data
excluded.media_recommendation: media recommendations — business content, not configuration
excluded.national_account_owner: national account ownership records — business data
excluded.ops.doc_whats_new_lead_creation: per-lead creation evidence (lead UUID, creation timestamp and original transaction ID) — business data. Migration 0766 backfills existing leads, and future inserts populate it through the lead trigger. A structure-only rebuild excludes leads and their watermark history, so this ledger must also start empty; business-data backups retain it with the leads.
excluded.ops.legacy_prior_staging_readback_allowl: a one-time legacy staging-replay allowlist; a fresh database has no legacy replay to allow
excluded.ops.rule_control_binding: per-rule history, not bounded internal control configuration; bin/schema-snapshot.sh names this table by name as one never to add
excluded.ops.rule_pack: 0291's only migration-time insert is a probe that asserts its own row does NOT survive; the table holds no migration-seeded rows. Runtime pack rows are outside this check's scope, which is migration-seeded rows only
excluded.ops.scac_policy_epoch: the policy epoch is derived runtime assurance evidence, not seed configuration. A fresh reconstructed database intentionally starts with no blessed epoch; SIEP-12 and SIEP-18 acceptance assert that state and require the real deferred refresh trigger to create the first cryptographically valid epoch only after nonempty reviewed doctrine and rule projections arrive
excluded.ops.service: observability service inventory — runtime state, rebuilt by the environment it describes
excluded.ops.source_merge_plan_scope: append-only per-accepted-plan source-merge authority history, not bounded configuration. Every row is transactionally captured from one human-accepted sourced plan and is foreign-key-bound to that operational work request, plan, acceptance receipt, and actor; the snapshot carries none of those sourced-plan parent rows. A fresh rebuild therefore correctly starts with no prior merge authority and captures new scope rows only when a future plan is accepted
excluded.ops.tour_conflict_resolution_receipt: per-tour conflict resolution receipts — business data
excluded.ops.tour_public_projection_fact: published tour projection facts — business data
excluded.ops.tour_public_projection_seal_receipt: tour projection seal receipts — business data
excluded.org_merge_log: a record of org identity merges performed on production — business history
excluded.record_flag: flags raised against business rows — per-row history
excluded.system_config: operational settings, not vocabulary, and the kind of table where a value that should never be committed can appear; staging sets its own
excluded.tool_call: the verb call ledger — runtime history
